evidence: Turner documents the kuṭhāra axe family with Prakrit kuḍhāra/kuhāḍa and explicitly discusses the ṭh–r versus h–ḍ metathesis. Comparanda include Punjabi kuhāṛā/kuhāṛī, Bengali kuṛul, Oriya kurhāṛi/kuṛāri, Gujarati kuvāṛī, Marathi kurhāḍ and Kotgarhi kəṛari. These survey forms preserve those regional axe stems, including masculine/feminine pairs and local initial voicing or reduced vowels; the family link does not assert a regular sound law for every local variant. Other axe names and extended or uncertain responses are excluded.

Turner gives Bihari and Maithili silauṭ beside Hindi silauṭ/silwaṭ and Nepali silauṭo, a stone for grinding spices, from śilāpaṭṭa stone slab. The Magahi survey silaut/silauti names that grinding implement under the broader elicitation gloss mortar. The feminine final vowel is ordinary local nominal variation, not a separate added component.

The fourth *udukkhala branch (Prakrit ukkhala/okkhala) explicitly includes Punjabi ukkhalī, Hindi ukhlī/okhlī, Gujarati ukhaḷ/ukhḷũ/ukhḷī and Marathi ukhaḷ. These survey mortar forms fit that reduced-initial ukh-/okh- series. The western forms with weakened or lost final l are qualified family comparisons, not claims that every local ending has an independently demonstrated historical derivation; pestle-glossed homophones and unrelated mortar names are excluded.

The first musala pestle branch gives Oriya musaḷa and the Bihari/Maithili mūsar/musarā series, alongside western Himalayan musal. Adivasi Oriya mvsūl and Jaunsari musar preserve these s-bearing pestle stems. Turner separates ś-bearing western Himalayan forms into a second branch; those and h-bearing forms with unresolved branch membership are not included here.
